lessons.title: How TIG Works on Aluminium
lessons.body: TIG welding uses a non-consumable tungsten electrode to create an arc that melts the aluminium. Unlike steel, aluminium conducts heat away fast, so you need higher amperage. A 3mm thick aluminium plate needs about 120-150 amps. You also need 100% argon gas, not CO2. The arc breaks the tough aluminium oxide layer, which melts at 2072Â°C while the aluminium itself melts at 660Â°C. Without the arc, the oxide would float on the molten pool and cause defects. You add filler rod manually with your other hand. In Africa, many workshops use inverter TIG machines like the ESAB or local brands. Set gas flow to 10-15 litres per minute. Use a 2% lanthanated tungsten electrode (grey tip) for AC welding. Keep a short arc lengthâabout 2-3mm. If you hear a crackling sound, your amperage is too low. If the pool looks dirty and black, you need more cleaning action (more AC balance). Practice on scrap aluminium before welding a real job. Clean the metal with a stainless steel brush dedicated to aluminium, then wipe with acetone. Never use a brush that touched steel. TIG on aluminium is slower than MIG but gives better control for thin sheets and repairs. In many African countries, small fabrication shops use TIG for window frames, water tanks, and motorcycle parts. The key is to watch the molten pool, not the arc. The pool should look shiny and fluid. If it looks like mercury, you are too cold. If it boils and spits, you are too hot. Adjust your foot pedal or machine settings accordingly.

lessons.title: AC vs DC and Why It Matters
lessons.body: Aluminium needs alternating current (AC) for TIG welding. DC (direct current) is for steel and stainless. Why? Because aluminium forms a hard oxide layer that melts at 2072Â°C, while the metal below melts at 660Â°C. AC switches polarity 50 or 60 times per second. On the positive half-cycle, the arc blasts the oxide away (cleaning action). On the negative half-cycle, it penetrates and melts the base metal. If you use DC on aluminium, the oxide stays and your weld looks like a dirty mess. Most TIG machines have an AC/DC switch. Set it to AC. Then adjust the AC balance or cleaning width. On older machines, this is a knob from 0 to 10. On modern inverters, it's a percentage. Start at 30% cleaning (70% penetration). If the weld is black and sooty, increase cleaning to 40-50%. If the tungsten ball gets too big and the arc wanders, reduce cleaning to 20-25%. The frequency control (if available) sets how fast AC alternates. Higher frequency (100-200 Hz) gives a tighter arc for thin metal. Lower frequency (50-60 Hz) gives a wider arc for thick sections. For most African workshops, 60 Hz is fine. Note: you cannot weld aluminium with a DC-only machine. If your machine only has DC, you need a spool gun MIG or a different machine. Many cheap TIG machines sold in local markets are DC-only. Check before you buy. A good AC/DC TIG machine for a small shop costs around $800-$1500. Brands like Miller, Lincoln, or Chinese equivalents like Andeli or Riland work. Always use pure argon gas. Argon/helium mixes can help on thick aluminium (over 6mm) but are expensive and hard to find in many African countries. Stick to pure argon.

lessons.title: Choosing Tungsten Electrodes
lessons.body: For aluminium TIG, you need a tungsten electrode that handles AC without splitting. The best choice is 2% lanthanated (grey tip) or 2% ceriated (orange tip). Pure tungsten (green tip) also works but balls up faster and can't handle high amps. Thoriated tungsten (red tip) is for DC steel weldingâdo not use it on aluminium because it spits and contaminates the weld. Choose the diameter based on amperage: 1.6mm for 15-80 amps, 2.4mm for 70-150 amps, 3.2mm for 140-250 amps. For most aluminium jobs in a small shop (3-6mm thick), use 2.4mm lanthanated. You need to ball the tip before welding. Set your machine to AC, set amperage to about 100-120, and strike an arc on a scrap piece of aluminium for 2-3 seconds. The tip will melt into a smooth ball. The ball should be about 1.5 times the electrode diameter. If the ball is too big, reduce cleaning action or lower amperage. If the ball is tiny, increase amperage. Keep the tungsten sharpened on a dedicated grinder. Use a fine grit (100-200) diamond wheel or a dedicated stone. Never use the same grinder for steel because contamination causes porosity. Sharpen lengthwise, not across. In Africa, you can buy lanthanated tungsten from welding supply shops in major cities like Lagos, Nairobi, Johannesburg, or Cairo. A pack of 10 electrodes costs $15-$30. Store them in a dry place. If the tip gets contaminated (dips into the pool), stop, break off the dirty end, re-ball, and continue. A contaminated tungsten will cause a wandering arc and dirty weld. Always keep spares.

lessons.title: Filler Rods for Aluminium
lessons.body: Aluminium filler rods come in different alloys. The most common for general welding is 4043 (5% silicon). It melts at a lower temperature (580-620Â°C) and flows well, giving a shiny weld. It's good for casting repairs and most 6000-series aluminium. But 4043 is softer and not heat-treatable. For structural work or 5000-series aluminium (like 5052 or 5083), use 5356 (5% magnesium). It's stronger and more corrosion-resistant but harder to feed and can crack if used on high-silicon castings. For 7000-series, use 4043 or 5356 depending on the base. In Africa, 4043 is the easiest to find and cheapest. A 1kg pack of 2.4mm rods costs $10-$20. For most jobs, use a rod diameter that matches your base metal thickness. For 3mm aluminium, use 2.4mm rod. For 6mm, use 3.2mm rod. Feed the rod into the leading edge of the pool at a 15-20Â° angle. Don't dip it into the arcâthat causes spatter and contamination. Push the rod in, then pull it out slightly. The rod should melt and flow into the pool. If the rod sticks, you're too cold. If it balls up and doesn't flow, you're too hot. Clean the rod with acetone before use. Store rods in a dry place. Never use filler rod for steel or stainless on aluminium. Keep separate. For thin aluminium (1-2mm), you can sometimes weld without filler (autogenous) if the fit-up is tight. But for most repairs, use filler. In many African workshops, welders use 4043 for everything. That works for non-critical jobs, but for structural parts like truck frames or boat hulls, use 5356. Always check the base metal grade if you can. If unknown, 4043 is a safe default.

lessons.title: Setting Up Your Machine
lessons.body: Set up your TIG machine correctly before you strike an arc. First, connect the ground clamp to a clean, bare metal part of your workpiece. For aluminium, grind off any paint or oxide where the clamp touches. Use a good quality clampâcheap ones overheat. Next, connect the torch. For AC TIG, the torch cable goes to the negative terminal (on most machines) and the ground to positive. But check your manualâsome inverters are different. Set the machine to AC. Set amperage based on thickness: 1.6mm = 60-80A, 3mm = 120-150A, 6mm = 200-250A. If you have a foot pedal, use it to control heat. If not, set amperage and use a switch. Set gas flow to 10-15 litres per minute (LPM). Use a flowmeter, not just a regulator. Too little gas gives porosity; too much causes turbulence and sucks in air. Set AC balance to 30% cleaning (or 70% penetration). If your machine has frequency, set to 60 Hz for thick, 100-150 Hz for thin. Install a 2.4mm lanthanated tungsten, ball it on scrap. Set the torch angle at 70-80Â° from the workpiece, pushing slightly forward. For filler, use 2.4mm 4043 rod. Wear a good helmet with shade 10-11 for aluminium (brighter than steel). Use clean glovesâdirty gloves contaminate. In Africa, power can be unstable. Use a voltage stabiliser or a generator if needed. A 200A TIG machine draws about 5-6 kW. Make sure your wiring can handle it. Never bypass the safety ground. Practice on scrap before welding a real part. Adjust settings as you go. If the weld is too cold, increase amps or reduce cleaning. If too hot, do the opposite.

lessons.title: Your First Bead on Aluminium
lessons.body: Before you weld a real part, practice on a scrap piece of 3mm aluminium. Clean it with a stainless brush and acetone. Set your machine: AC, 120 amps, 30% cleaning, 12 LPM argon, 2.4mm lanthanated tungsten (balled), 2.4mm 4043 filler. Put on your helmet (shade 10), gloves, and long sleeves. Rest your torch hand on the table for stability. Hold the torch at 75Â° angle, pointing forward. Touch the tungsten to the metal to start the arc (or use high-frequency start if available). Once the arc starts, lift to 2-3mm arc length. Watch the pool form. It should look shiny and fluid. If it looks like a mirror, you're too coldâincrease amps. If it boils and spits, you're too hotâreduce amps or increase travel speed. Move the torch forward slowly, about 2-3mm per second. Dip the filler rod into the leading edge of the pool, then pull it out. Do this rhythmically: move, dip, move, dip. The bead should be about 4-6mm wide. Don't worry if it's ugly at first. After you finish, let it cool, then inspect. A good bead has even ripples, no holes, no black soot. If you see black soot, increase cleaning action or reduce amperage. If you see holes (porosity), increase gas flow or clean the metal better. Practice for at least an hour on scrap. Then try a butt joint on two pieces of 3mm aluminium. Tack both ends first. Weld from one end to the other. Use a backstep technique (weld 50mm, then start 50mm back) to control distortion. Aluminium warps easily, so clamp your work. In Africa, many welders learn by doing. Don't be afraid to make mistakes. Each bead teaches you something. Keep your tungsten sharp and your metal clean. That's 80% of the battle.

quiz.q: What type of current is required for TIG welding aluminium?
quiz.explanation: AC is needed to break up the aluminium oxide layer and provide cleaning action.

quiz.q: Why is pure argon used as shielding gas for TIG welding aluminium?
options: A) It is cheaper than CO2
B) It provides good cleaning action and arc stability
C) It adds carbon to the weld
D) It prevents oxidation better than helium
quiz.explanation: Argon is inert and works well with AC for aluminium, providing stable arc and cleaning.

quiz.q: What is the approximate melting point of aluminium oxide?
quiz.explanation: Aluminium oxide melts at about 2072Â°C, much higher than aluminium metal.

quiz.q: Which tungsten electrode type is recommended for AC TIG welding of aluminium?
quiz.explanation: Lanthanated tungsten handles AC current well and resists contamination.

quiz.q: What should you do before welding aluminium to remove the oxide layer?
options: B) Brush with a stainless steel brush and wipe with acetone
quiz.explanation: A dedicated stainless brush removes oxide, and acetone removes oils and dirt.

quiz.q: What is the typical amperage range for TIG welding 3mm thick aluminium?
quiz.explanation: 3mm aluminium requires about 120-150 amps for proper penetration.

quiz.q: What does the AC balance control do on a TIG machine?
options: B) Sets the ratio of cleaning to penetration
quiz.explanation: AC balance determines how much time is spent on positive (cleaning) vs negative (penetration) half-cycle.

quiz.q: Which filler rod is most common for general aluminium TIG welding?
quiz.explanation: 4043 (5% silicon) is the most widely used and easy to find in Africa.

quiz.q: What is the recommended gas flow rate for TIG welding aluminium?
quiz.explanation: 10-15 litres per minute provides adequate shielding without turbulence.

quiz.q: What happens if you use DC instead of AC when TIG welding aluminium?
options: B) The oxide layer is not removed and the weld is dirty
C) The arc is more stable
quiz.explanation: DC lacks the cleaning action of AC, so the oxide remains and causes a poor weld.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of balling the tungsten electrode?
options: A) To make it last longer
B) To spread the arc and reduce penetration
quiz.explanation: A balled tip on AC gives a wider arc and softer cleaning action.

quiz.q: Which tungsten diameter is suitable for 70-150 amps?
quiz.explanation: 2.4mm tungsten handles 70-150 amps, ideal for most aluminium jobs.

quiz.q: What should you do if your tungsten gets contaminated?
options: B) Break off the dirty end and re-ball
quiz.explanation: Contaminated tungsten causes arc wander and dirty welds, so it must be cleaned or replaced.

quiz.q: For 5000-series aluminium, which filler rod is recommended?
quiz.explanation: 5356 (5% magnesium) matches the strength and corrosion resistance of 5000-series base metal.

quiz.q: What is the correct torch angle for TIG welding aluminium?
quiz.explanation: A 70-80Â° angle allows good visibility and filler rod access.

quiz.q: What should you check before welding if your machine has a foot pedal?
options: A) That it is plugged in
B) That it controls amperage smoothly
C) That it is set to maximum
quiz.explanation: A foot pedal should give smooth amperage control for precise heat management.

quiz.q: What is the recommended shade for a TIG welding helmet on aluminium?
quiz.explanation: Shade 10-11 protects eyes while allowing clear view of the bright aluminium pool.

quiz.q: Why is it important to use a dedicated stainless steel brush for aluminium?
options: B) To avoid contamination from steel particles
quiz.explanation: Steel particles embedded in aluminium cause rust and porosity.

quiz.q: What does a shiny, fluid weld pool indicate?
quiz.explanation: A shiny pool means the aluminium is molten and flowing properly.

quiz.q: What is the recommended travel speed for a first bead on 3mm aluminium?
quiz.explanation: 2-3mm per second allows proper fusion without burning through.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of tack welding before running a full bead?
options: B) To hold the pieces in alignment and reduce distortion
quiz.explanation: Tacks keep parts aligned and control warping during welding.

quiz.q: Which of these is a sign of too little gas flow?
quiz.explanation: Inadequate shielding causes atmospheric contamination and porosity.

quiz.q: What is the typical cost of a 1kg pack of 2.4mm 4043 filler rods in Africa?
quiz.explanation: 4043 rods are affordable and widely available in major African cities.

quiz.q: What should you do if your weld has a black sooty appearance?
quiz.explanation: Black soot indicates insufficient cleaning action; increase AC balance.

quiz.q: What is the correct arc length for TIG welding aluminium?
quiz.explanation: A short arc of 2-3mm maintains stable arc and good shielding.

quiz.q: Why should you avoid using thoriated tungsten on aluminium?
options: B) It spits and contaminates the weld
quiz.explanation: Thoriated tungsten is designed for DC and performs poorly on AC aluminium.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a voltage stabiliser in African workshops?
options: B) To protect the machine from power fluctuations
quiz.explanation: Unstable power can damage TIG machines; a stabiliser ensures consistent voltage.

quiz.q: What is the recommended frequency setting for thin aluminium (1-2mm)?
quiz.explanation: Higher frequency gives a tighter arc, better for thin material.

quiz.q: What should you do if the filler rod sticks to the workpiece?
quiz.explanation: Sticking indicates the pool is too cold; increase amperage.

quiz.q: What is the main advantage of TIG welding over MIG for aluminium?
options: B) Better control and cleaner welds
quiz.explanation: TIG offers precise heat control and superior weld quality, especially on thin or critical parts.
